Qualtrics Assignment #2 - Experimentation

Aldo Naranjo
2026-09-30

Overview

This assignment documents the completed Social Media Opinion Leader-Experimental Design survey in Qualtrics. The work focused on experimental random assignment, routing participants to the correct treatment condition, improving the measurement of social-media usage, and making three additional questionnaire improvements.

1. Random Assignment and Survey Flow

The experiment uses a between-subjects design so that each participant sees only one of two treatment conditions: either the ads block or the social_media_review block.

The Survey Flow first assigns each respondent an id. Immediately afterward, a Randomizer randomly presents 1 of two Embedded Data elements and uses Evenly Present Elements to keep the groups approximately balanced.

  • Ad Type = reviewer
  • Ad Type = ads

Later in the Survey Flow, two Branch elements route respondents based on the assigned value of Ad Type.

  • If Ad Type = ads, the respondent sees the ads block.
  • If Ad Type = reviewer, the respondent sees the social_media_review block.
  • After either treatment, all respondents continue to the DV, Purchasing Behavior, and Demographics blocks.

The randomization was tested in Preview mode several times. Across three attempts, both treatment conditions appeared, confirming that the random assignment and branching worked as intended.

2. Improvement of Q2.2: Social-Media Usage by Platform

The original Q2.2 measured total social-media usage as a whole. It was revised so that respondents first identify all social-media platforms they use by selecting multiple answers.

A new Matrix Table question was then added immediately after Q2.2. The Carry Forward Statements function carries forward only the platforms selected in Q2.2. This means each respondent reports a separate daily usage rate only for the platforms they actually use.

  • 1 hour or less per day
  • 1–2 hours per day
  • 3–4 hours per day
  • 4–5 hours per day
  • 5 or more hours per day

This approach is better than a single overall usage question because it produces a separate usage measure for each selected social-media platform.

3. Three Additional Questionnaire Improvements

Improvement 1: Q9.4 Other Ethnicity Text Entry

The Others response in Q9.4 was changed to Others (please specify) and a text-entry field was enabled.

This improves the questionnaire because an "Other" response is no longer ambiguous; respondents can provide the specific category that applies to them.

Improvement 2: Q8.4 Frequency Scale

Q8.4 asks, "How often do you purchase a product or service because of traditional advertising?" The original scale mixed frequency wording with amount wording. The scale was revised to a consistent frequency continuum:

  • Never
  • Rarely
  • Occasionally
  • Often
  • Very Often

This improves measurement consistency because all response options now answer the same "How often" question.

Improvement 3: Q8.5 Likelihood Scale Order

Q8.5 asks how likely a respondent would be to recommend a product or service seen on social media. The response order was changed to run consistently from low likelihood to high likelihood:

  • Very unlikely
  • Unlikely
  • Neutral
  • Likely
  • Very likely

This creates a clearer low-to-high progression and makes the scale easier to interpret during analysis.

Final Verification

The completed survey was reviewed in Qualtrics Preview mode. The Carry Forward question displayed only the platforms selected by the respondent, and the experimental treatment changed across repeated preview attempts. These checks confirmed that the main programmed functions were working correctly.
